parts.note: the Latin plural for slips in a printed text is the word printers still use for a list of corrections

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's howlers in a Latin homework exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a complaint about a poor translation, but it is asking for the Latin word that translates as mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin noun is borrowed into English for a list of printing slips, literally meaning things gone astray.

indicators.note: set here means arranged or put in order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A precedent established long ago by the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set by' reads as 'established by'; in fact 'set' is the signal to rearrange ANCIENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited as an illustration, a synonym for example.

clue.text: Place of interest it's the custom to be silent going round

indicators.note: going round says the word for silence wraps around the word for custom

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keeping mum
use is custom or habit, as in long usage

explanation.surface: A gallery or library where everyone is expected to stay quiet as they walk round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep mum' is a British idiom for staying quiet; 'it's the' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum is a typical visitor attraction, the kind of site tourist maps mark as of interest.

parts.note: the first Sherlock Holmes story is titled A Study in a certain red, so his study has that colour

explanation.surface: Wondering how the detective's den is decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' is not a room but the title of Conan Doyle's first Holmes novel, A Study in Scarlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright red shade, named in the title of the first Holmes novel.

parts.note: a gin is also a kind of trap for animals, so catching with one means using these

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' suggests the drink, but a gin trap is a spring trap for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch in a trap or noose, the verb form of a hunting device.

clue.text: Chelsea's opener precedes painful play in big match

indicators.note: precedes says the first letter comes before the rest in the answer
the opener of a word is its first letter, here of the football club name
play suggests the letters move about freely, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Chelsea's star striker opens the scoring amid a scrappy, painful contest in a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: The CUP FINAL is the deciding match of a football knockout competition such as England's FA Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: The deciding game of a knockout tournament is a major sporting occasion.

clue.text: Say it, for example, before church

indicators.note: before places the grammatical term ahead of the church abbreviation

parts.note: it is an example of a pronoun, a word standing in for a noun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Instructions to declare something before a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is not the thing to be said but a sample pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate or utter words, a synonym for say.

clue.text: Where one may put the chalk before break, at the right moment

definitions.text: Where one may put the chalk before break
definitions.meaning: a snooker player chalks the tip of the stick before the opening shot, the break
exactly on time, like an actor coming in at the signal

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, the break is the first shot of a frame, and the chalk is rubbed onto the cue's tip.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor entering at the prompt arrives exactly when required, hence punctually.

parts.note: keen as a noun means a loud wail, so a cry raised before fighting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like the adjective eager, but it is the noun meaning a wailing cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout raised by troops charging into combat is a call made for fighting.

clue.text: Boat with half the crew in the stern

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters of crew

parts.note: aft means at the stern, the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A vessel with some sailors gathered at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft is any vessel, especially a small boat.

clue.text: It comes before the final passion

definitions.meaning: a preliminary qualifying round in a competition precedes the deciding race
strong feeling or intensity, as in the warmth of an argument

explanation.walkthrough: In athletics or swimming, heats are qualifying races held before the final.
explanation.definitionFit: The qualifying race before a final, and also intense emotion, as in the fervour of the moment.

clue.text: Keep quiet about silver and nitrogen in the bottle

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for silence surrounds the two element symbols

parts.note: mum means quiet, as in keep mum
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Secretly stashing precious metal and gas inside a flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a large wine bottle holding two standard bottles' worth.

parts.note: even so means nevertheless or still

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling that a church service was bad all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican evening prayer service, a church service sung at dusk.

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word for cover is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A model who has given up magazine covers faces a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a hard choice between two options, a kind of problem.

clue.text: Naughty child to lie when in trouble, being insolent

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: in trouble suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A misbehaving youngster caught out telling lies and being cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and disrespectful behaviour is impoliteness, close to insolence.

definitions.meaning: principal or chief, as in the chief road
the open ocean, a poetic sense
strength, as in the phrase with might and ...

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a naval nation, but the clue is three definitions of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means chief, the open ocean, and physical strength in the old phrase with might and main.

parts.note: a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce car

explanation.surface: A tram crawling along, perhaps the streetcar named Desire.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'streetcar' must be split into two halves; the car is a Rolls-Royce, a British luxury make.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble or walk at leisure is to move along slowly.

parts.note: go by means pass rather than travel, as a car passes a slower vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go by car' looks like travel by car; read 'go by' as pass, and a car passing another does this.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing a slower vehicle on the road, typically in a car.

clue.text: Places visited on holiday, or between holidays

indicators.note: between puts the little word inside the word for breaks

parts.note: rests are breaks or holidays

explanation.surface: Holiday destinations, or what lies between one break and the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside and ski towns where people take vacations are popular destinations.

clue.text: A quiet river location, well chosen

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
the Po is Italy's longest river
a site is a location

explanation.surface: An estate agent praising a peaceful riverside spot as a good pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt or fitting, describing a remark that suits the occasion exactly.

parts.note: firm means company, so its base is the place where the company works

explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm base' suggests solid foundations; read 'firm' as company.
explanation.definitionFit: The workplace or headquarters of a business is where it is based.

indicators.note: comes first puts the verb for noticing ahead of the little word

parts.note: to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A doctor's note: the pimple appears before it becomes a boil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boil' and 'spot' suggest skin complaints, but boil is a verb and spot means notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To bubble with heat or anger, as water does at boiling point.

definitions.meaning: to silence someone, a rude command for quiet
locked away, confined in a cell

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to make someone quiet and to confine them behind locked doors.

clue.text: Poor firm later making a profit

indicators.note: later puts the word for profit after the word for firm

parts.note: hard means firm or solid
up means ahead or in profit, as in being up on a deal

explanation.surface: A struggling company that later turns a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Short of money, an informal idiom for poor.

parts.note: Labour is the British party of the political left

explanation.surface: A split between Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Conservative and Labour are Britain's two main parties, of the right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split or crack, a synonym for rift.

definitions.meaning: the Trumpet ... by Jeremiah Clarke is a famous wedding piece
not pressed into service, freely given rather than forced

explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' is not admiring but forced into service, as sailors were press-ganged.
explanation.definitionFit: A church organ or trumpet solo of this name, and an adjective for freely offered work.

clue.text: Shuffle the cards dishonestly and make a pile

definitions.meaning: to arrange a deck so as to cheat, as in a rigged deck
to heap things up one on another

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to rig a deck of cards and to heap things neatly.

indicators.note: including means the word for fat contains the word for crease

parts.note: stout means fat or portly
a ruck is a wrinkle or crease in fabric

explanation.surface: Someone trimming fat and smoothing creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleted or crossed out, as a line through text removes it.
